steps.name: Sample structure QC and sample_01 depth adjudication
caveats: A sample with a library size several times below the median must be kept through QC, inspected on the PCA and the distance heatmap, and removed only with a stated reason — count models down-weight low depth through the size factor, so removal is a judgment, not a default
With only 12 samples the PCA is easily dominated by one aberrant sample; inspect PC1 and PC2 and also the plot with sample_01 excluded before concluding the cohort does not separate
steps.context: Bulk RNA-seq, Homo sapiens skin, atopic dermatitis lesional vs control, 6 vs 6, unpaired, single batch, raw gene-level counts from Salmon. The data profile flags sample_01 as having a library size about 4x below the median. This step exists to make the exclusion decision auditable rather than implicit.
steps.question: Do the 12 skin samples separate by condition (AD lesional vs control), and does sample_01 — whose library is about 4x below the median — behave as a usable low-depth sample or as a structural outlier that must be excluded with a stated reason?

grounding.reason: Raw counts before a model: blind VST, PCA on top 500 variable genes and sample-distance heatmap per R-0033@40bf; the low-depth sample_01 is kept, inspected and reported rather than dropped, per the warn flag R-0008@440d.

PCA on the 500 most variable genes
Do not delete sample_01 silently; depth alone is not a valid exclusion reason
Do not pre-scale, pre-normalize, or transform counts before the model
Report sample_01's library size and detected genes beside those of the other 11 samples
steps.description: Load /eval-four-arms-with-two-group-n6-enrich-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12,000 genes x 12 samples, gene symbol in the first column) and /eval-four-arms-with-two-group-n6-enrich-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (12 rows, condition column). steps.name: DESeq2 Wald test, lesional vs control, with apeglm shrinkage
caveats: n=6 per group has power for moderate-to-large effects only; absence of a gene from the DE list is not evidence of no change

If the p-value histogram is not flat-with-a-left-peak (a hill in the middle, or a rise toward 1), the BH-adjusted values are not reliable and this must be reported rather than passed over
steps.context: 12,000 genes x 12 samples, Salmon gene-level raw counts already summarised to gene symbols — the transcript-level tximport length-offset route is not available because only the summed gene count matrix was provided; note this in the output, since without length offsets a gene whose isoform usage shifts can be mis-called. steps.question: Which genes are differentially expressed in atopic dermatitis lesional skin versus control skin at FDR 5%, and how much does the shallow sample_01 library change that answer?

grounding.reason: Raw counts, fixed-effects two-group design at 6 replicates per group: DESeq2 Wald with apeglm shrinkage (R-0001@9a17, R-0009@f54e), minimal pre-filter then independent filtering (R-0029@fa6d), explicit reference level and named contrast (R-0036@9786), BH at alpha 0.05 (R-0010@91a5); R-0018@a472 length offsets cannot be applied because only gene-level sums were supplied, and the step states that.

constraints: Pre-filter minimally: min_count = 10 in min_samples = 6; do not raise the threshold
Do not pre-normalize the counts — median-of-ratios size factors are estimated inside DESeq2
Set the reference level explicitly; do not rely on alphabetical ordering of factor levels
Test = Wald; alpha passed to results() must equal the 0.05 reporting cutoff
Independent filtering stays ON; BH adjustment
Keep the DESeq2 count-outlier behaviour on (flag and set p to NA) and report the flagged count
Shrink with apeglm on the condition coefficient; keep the unshrunken estimate in the table beside it
Select DE genes by adjusted p-value only — never by unadjusted p-value and never by fold change alone

steps.description: Pre-filter genes to those with at least 10 counts in at least 6 samples (the smallest group size), then fit DESeq2 on the raw counts with design ~ condition, setting control as the explicit reference level so the contrast c('condition','lesional','control') gives positive log2 fold changes for genes up in lesional skin. Run the Wald test, extract results with alpha = 0.05 and independent filtering on, and inspect the histogram of unadjusted p-values before trusting the BH adjustment — report its shape. Apply apeglm shrinkage to the condition coefficient and keep both the unshrunken and shrunken log2 fold changes plus lfcSE in the output table. Report the count of genes with NA p-values from the Cook's-distance outlier flag separately from those removed by independent filtering (at 6 replicates per cell DESeq2 flags rather than replaces outliers). The p-value histogram is produced and its shape described before the BH adjustment is trusted
The number of genes with NA padj from the outlier flag is reported separately from those removed by independent filtering

caveats: Method disagreement grows at low counts and low replicate numbers — expect the non-overlapping genes to be concentrated among low-expression genes and say so

steps.question: Which of the DESeq2 lesional-vs-control calls are reproduced by an independent count model, and which are method-specific?

grounding.reason: edgeR quasi-likelihood is the named alternative to the DESeq2 Wald test at 2-11 replicates per group (R-0001@9a17); R-0042@54e1 requires reporting both counts and the intersection as the high-confidence set.

constraints: Use the same filtered gene set as T1S2 so the two methods are compared on identical input
TMM normalization factors inside the edgeR model; no pre-scaled counts
BH adjustment at FDR 0.05, matching the DESeq2 cutoff
Report the overlap, not the union
steps.description: Fit the same contrast with edgeR on the same filtered count matrix: TMM normalization factors, glmQLFit with robust dispersion, and glmQLFTest for lesional vs control, BH-adjusted at FDR 5%. acceptance_criteria: edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test results for the lesional-vs-control contrast are written for all tested genes

steps.name: Preranked hallmark GSEA on the Wald statistic
caveats: Enrichment results are strongly method-dependent; report hallmark hits as hypotheses for follow-up, not as demonstrated mechanism
GO Biological Process is a nested hierarchy — parent and child sets share members, so expect blocks of correlated hits and collapse them before quoting a count
Gene length and expression level bias enrichment; using the tested genes as the universe removes only the detection component of that bias
steps.context: Human atopic dermatitis lesional vs control skin. Hallmark is the required first collection for a human dataset. Reactome C2:CP is the canonical second collection but is NOT staged in this environment; the staged MSigDB C5 GO Biological Process sets are used as the second pass instead, and that substitution must be stated in the output. Confirm the hallmark collection is present at run time and report its version; if it is absent the step must stop and say so rather than substituting a different organism's sets.
steps.question: Which MSigDB hallmark pathways are coordinately up or down in atopic dermatitis lesional skin versus control, and which leading-edge genes drive each one?

grounding.reason: Human dataset: preranked fgsea on the full tested list against MSigDB Hallmark first (R-0107@976c, R-0048@500d). For the disputed ranking metric R-0108@409f this plan chooses the DESeq2 Wald statistic, because it scales the effect by its uncertainty and avoids the tie saturation of a signed p-value (R-0099@0a77). R-0098@d01b names Reactome as the second collection but it is not staged here, so staged GO BP substitutes and the step states the substitution.

constraints: Rank metric = the DESeq2 Wald statistic (stat); this is the plan's stated choice among the disputed alternatives, chosen because it scales the effect by its uncertainty
Do not rank by the unshrunken log2 fold change alone, and do not rank by a signed p-value that saturates and creates ties
Never threshold the gene list before the ranked test
Universe = the genes tested in T1S2, not the whole genome or the whole annotation
min set size 15, max 500, applied after intersecting each set with the tested genes
Use the HUMAN hallmark collection — the mouse hallmark file is also present in this environment and must not be used
Collapse redundant significant sets and report one representative per group; keep the full table as a supplement
Do not run an over-representation test on the significant gene list if it holds fewer than about 50 genes
Report the collection name, its version, the rank metric, the universe and the size window with the results
steps.description: Take the full T1S2 results table for every tested gene — not a thresholded subset — and rank genes by the DESeq2 Wald statistic (the `stat` column), which is the stated choice of ranking metric for this plan. Restrict sets to 15-500 members after intersecting with the tested genes. BH-adjust across sets, report NES, padj, set size, and the leading-edge genes of every significant set with each member's Wald statistic. The human MSigDB hallmark collection is used with its version reported, and gene-symbol matching is direct with the unmapped share stated
Gene sets are restricted to 15-500 members after intersection with the tested genes, and the window is reported
A results table with NES, pval, BH-adjusted padj, set size and leading-edge genes is written for all 50 hallmark sets
Leading-edge genes of each significant set are listed with their Wald statistics, and overlapping leading edges between reported sets are marked
A second preranked pass against human GO Biological Process is reported, with the note that Reactome was not available in this environment
The permutation seed is recorded

steps.name: Integrated report with diagnostics and reproducibility record
caveats: Do not let a compelling pathway narrative outrun the gene-level evidence; if the DE list is short or the p-value histogram was irregular, that must lead the interpretation rather than sit in a footnote
steps.context: Synthesis of T1S1 (QC and the sample_01 verdict), T1S2 (DESeq2 DE and the depth sensitivity analysis), T1S2b (edgeR overlap) and T2S1 (hallmark and GO GSEA).
steps.question: What is the defensible answer to 'which genes and which hallmark pathways change between AD lesional and control skin', with the sample_01 depth decision and every methodological limit stated?

grounding.reason: Report content follows the returned report-step rules: method/version/design/threshold disclosure (R-0041@059a), MA and dispersion diagnostics (R-0087@c53d), shrunken and unshrunken effects side by side (R-0085@c24d), two-method overlap (R-0042@54e1), enrichment provenance and method-dependence caveat (R-0051@01ca, R-0055@107a), leading edge per set (R-0105@c4a8), reproducibility record (R-0086@becf).

constraints: Rank the gene table by the shrunken log2 fold change, never by the unshrunken value alone
Keep the p-values from the unshrunken fit and name the shrinkage estimator in the table header
Report the DESeq2/edgeR overlap, not the union
State that enrichment results depend on the method chosen and present pathway hits as hypotheses
Store the reproducibility record with the results, not as a separate note
Do not state a biological conclusion that the FDR-adjusted results do not support
steps.description: Assemble a single report. Open with the design (6 lesional vs 6 control human skin, unpaired, single batch, Salmon gene-level counts, 12,000 genes before filtering), the methods and package versions, the design formula and named contrast, the thresholds, the number of genes tested after filtering, and the number of DE genes. Include the two fit diagnostics — the MA plot with significant genes marked and the dispersion-estimate plot — before any gene table, and say what each shows. Give the gene table with unshrunken log2FoldChange, apeglm-shrunken log2FoldChange and lfcSE side by side, ranked by the shrunken value; the p-values come from the unshrunken fit and shrinkage does not change the test. Report the DESeq2 / edgeR overlap from T1S2b as the high-confidence set. Report the hallmark GSEA table with database version, rank metric (Wald statistic), universe, size window and the leading-edge genes of each significant set, plus the GO BP second pass and the note that Reactome was unavailable. State the sample_01 verdict, its stated reason, and the with/without sensitivity result. Close with the limitations: n=6 per group detects moderate-to-large effects only, no independent validation cohort, enrichment is method-dependent, and gene-level counts preclude isoform-length offsets. Attach the full reproducibility record: sessionInfo, all package versions, the permutation seed, and the gene set collection version.
acceptance_criteria: The report names the method, package versions, design formula, contrast direction, thresholds, number of genes tested after filtering, and number of DE genes
MA plot and dispersion plot appear before the gene tables, each with a caption stating what it shows
The gene table carries unshrunken LFC, shrunken LFC and lfcSE together, ranked by the shrunken value
The DESeq2/edgeR intersection is reported as the high-confidence set with both individual counts
The enrichment section states the collection and version, the rank metric, the universe, the size window, and lists leading-edge genes per significant set
The sample_01 keep/drop verdict, its reason, and the with/without sensitivity comparison are stated explicitly
A limitations section states the n=6 power limit, the absence of a validation cohort, the method-dependence of enrichment, and the missing isoform length offsets
sessionInfo, package versions, the seed, and the gene set collection version are stored with the results

plan.title: AD lesional vs control DE + hallmark GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a 12,000-gene x 12-sample raw integer count matrix from Salmon (counts.csv, gene symbols in the first column) with a 12-row metadata table carrying a single condition column: 6 atopic dermatitis lesional skin samples vs 6 controls, unpaired, single batch, Homo sapiens. The research question has two parts — which genes change, and which hallmark pathways change — plus an explicit concern about one shallow library (sample_01, roughly 4x below median depth).

The design is a clean two-group fixed-effects contrast at n=6 per group, which is squarely in the range where a negative-binomial count model with empirical-Bayes dispersion shrinkage is the appropriate test. Step T1S1 runs sample-structure QC first and specifically resolves the sample_01 question: library size and detected-gene counts for all 12 samples, blind VST, PCA on the top 500 variable genes, and a sample-distance heatmap. The decision rule is stated in advance — depth alone is not grounds for exclusion, because DESeq2 size factors already down-weight a shallow library and widen its confidence intervals; sample_01 is dropped only if it is also a structural outlier (mis-grouping on PCA, aberrant distance profile, or collapsed gene detection), and the reason must be stated. T1S2 then fits the model on the full 12 samples with control as the explicit reference level so a positive log2 fold change means higher in lesional, and it repeats the fit without sample_01 as a sensitivity analysis so the reader can see exactly how much the shallow library moves the result rather than trusting an unexamined judgment call. T1S2b adds an edgeR quasi-likelihood fit as an independent method; at 6 replicates per group the two tools agree on most genes but not all, and the intersection is the defensible high-confidence set.

T2S1 answers the pathway half. Enrichment runs as preranked GSEA on the full list of tested genes ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic — not on a thresholded gene list — against the staged MSigDB human hallmark collection (50 sets, HGNC symbols, matching the gene-symbol identifier space of counts.csv, so no cross-species mapping and no identifier translation are needed). The Wald statistic is the stated choice for the ranking metric among the defensible alternatives, because it scales the effect by its uncertainty and so does not put noisy low-count genes at the top. Human Reactome sets are not staged in this environment; GO Biological Process (MSigDB C5, staged) serves as the second, mechanism-level collection, and that substitution is recorded rather than silently made. T1S3 assembles the report with the fit diagnostics, both shrunken and unshrunken effect sizes, the leading-edge genes of each significant set, the sample_01 decision and its sensitivity result, and the full reproducibility record.

The honest limits: n=6 per group detects moderate-to-large effects only, one dataset with no independent validation cohort, and enrichment results are known to depend on the method chosen — pathway hits are hypotheses for follow-up, not established mechanism.

steps.method: Sample structure QC: blind VST, PCA on top 500 variable genes, sample distance heatmap, library size and detected gene table
Keep genes with at least 10 counts in at least 6 samples (smallest group size)
~ condition with control as explicit reference level; contrast condition lesional vs control
Benjamini-Hochberg with independent filtering, p-value histogram inspected
fgsea preranked GSEA on the DESeq2 Wald statistic against MSigDB Hallmark human, then GO BP as second collection
Report with MA plot, dispersion plot, effect columns, leading edge genes, session info

steps.question: Which of the DESeq2 lesional-vs-control calls are reproduced by an independent count model, and which are method-specific?
steps.description: Fit the same contrast with edgeR on the same filtered count matrix: TMM normalization factors, glmQLFit with robust dispersion, and glmQLFTest for lesional vs control, BH-adjusted at FDR 5%. Report the number of significant genes from edgeR, the number from DESeq2 (read from T1S2), and the size of their intersection. Treat the intersection as the high-confidence set and list the method-specific genes as a secondary set naming which method called each. Do not present the union as the result. Produce a scatter of the two log fold-change estimates for the tested genes.
steps.context: Two independent count models on the same 6-vs-6 design. At this replicate number DESeq2 and edgeR agree on most genes, with disagreement concentrated at low counts — which is exactly where the shallow sample_01 library matters most.
acceptance_criteria: edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test results for the lesional-vs-control contrast are written for all tested genes
The DESeq2 count, the edgeR count, and the intersection size are reported as three explicit numbers
The intersection is labelled the high-confidence set and the method-specific genes are listed separately with the calling method named
The union is not presented as the primary result
constraints: Use the same filtered gene set as T1S2 so the two methods are compared on identical input
TMM normalization factors inside the edgeR model; no pre-scaled counts
BH adjustment at FDR 0.05, matching the DESeq2 cutoff
Report the overlap, not the union
caveats: Method disagreement grows at low counts and low replicate numbers — expect the non-overlapping genes to be concentrated among low-expression genes and say so

grounding.reason: edgeR quasi-likelihood is the named alternative to the DESeq2 Wald test at 2-11 replicates per group (R-0001@9a17); R-0042@54e1 requires reporting both counts and the intersection as the high-confidence set.

steps.name: Preranked hallmark GSEA on the Wald statistic
steps.question: Which MSigDB hallmark pathways are coordinately up or down in atopic dermatitis lesional skin versus control, and which leading-edge genes drive each one?
steps.description: Take the full T1S2 results table for every tested gene — not a thresholded subset — and rank genes by the DESeq2 Wald statistic (the `stat` column), which is the stated choice of ranking metric for this plan. Run fgsea against the human MSigDB hallmark gene set collection (50 sets, HGNC gene symbols), which the environment holds; the counts matrix already uses gene symbols, so intersect directly with no identifier translation, and report the share of tested genes that do not appear in any hallmark set. Restrict sets to 15-500 members after intersecting with the tested genes. BH-adjust across sets, report NES, padj, set size, and the leading-edge genes of every significant set with each member's Wald statistic. Collapse sets whose leading edges overlap substantially into groups and report one representative per group, keeping the full table as a supplement. Then run the same preranked test against the human GO Biological Process collection as a second, mechanism-level pass and report the top sets. Set and record a random seed for the permutation step. If fewer than about 50 genes reached significance in T1S2, state that number and note that this is precisely why the ranked method rather than an over-representation test on a short list is being used.
steps.context: Human atopic dermatitis lesional vs control skin. Hallmark is the required first collection for a human dataset. Reactome C2:CP is the canonical second collection but is NOT staged in this environment; the staged MSigDB C5 GO Biological Process sets are used as the second pass instead, and that substitution must be stated in the output. Confirm the hallmark collection is present at run time and report its version; if it is absent the step must stop and say so rather than substituting a different organism's sets.
acceptance_criteria: fgsea is run on the FULL ranked list of tested genes, ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic — no significance or fold-change cutoff is applied before ranking
The human MSigDB hallmark collection is used with its version reported, and gene-symbol matching is direct with the unmapped share stated
Gene sets are restricted to 15-500 members after intersection with the tested genes, and the window is reported
A results table with NES, pval, BH-adjusted padj, set size and leading-edge genes is written for all 50 hallmark sets
Leading-edge genes of each significant set are listed with their Wald statistics, and overlapping leading edges between reported sets are marked
A second preranked pass against human GO Biological Process is reported, with the note that Reactome was not available in this environment
The permutation seed is recorded
constraints: Rank metric = the DESeq2 Wald statistic (stat); this is the plan's stated choice among the disputed alternatives, chosen because it scales the effect by its uncertainty
Do not rank by the unshrunken log2 fold change alone, and do not rank by a signed p-value that saturates and creates ties
Never threshold the gene list before the ranked test
Universe = the genes tested in T1S2, not the whole genome or the whole annotation
min set size 15, max 500, applied after intersecting each set with the tested genes
Use the HUMAN hallmark collection — the mouse hallmark file is also present in this environment and must not be used
Collapse redundant significant sets and report one representative per group; keep the full table as a supplement
Do not run an over-representation test on the significant gene list if it holds fewer than about 50 genes
Report the collection name, its version, the rank metric, the universe and the size window with the results
caveats: Enrichment results are strongly method-dependent; report hallmark hits as hypotheses for follow-up, not as demonstrated mechanism
GO Biological Process is a nested hierarchy — parent and child sets share members, so expect blocks of correlated hits and collapse them before quoting a count
Gene length and expression level bias enrichment; using the tested genes as the universe removes only the detection component of that bias

grounding.reason: Human dataset: preranked fgsea on the full tested list against MSigDB Hallmark first (R-0107@976c, R-0048@500d). For the disputed ranking metric R-0108@409f this plan chooses the DESeq2 Wald statistic, because it scales the effect by its uncertainty and avoids the tie saturation of a signed p-value (R-0099@0a77). R-0098@d01b names Reactome as the second collection but it is not staged here, so staged GO BP substitutes and the step states the substitution.

steps.name: Integrated report with diagnostics and reproducibility record
steps.question: What is the defensible answer to 'which genes and which hallmark pathways change between AD lesional and control skin', with the sample_01 depth decision and every methodological limit stated?
steps.description: Assemble a single report. Open with the design (6 lesional vs 6 control human skin, unpaired, single batch, Salmon gene-level counts, 12,000 genes before filtering), the methods and package versions, the design formula and named contrast, the thresholds, the number of genes tested after filtering, and the number of DE genes. Include the two fit diagnostics — the MA plot with significant genes marked and the dispersion-estimate plot — before any gene table, and say what each shows. Give the gene table with unshrunken log2FoldChange, apeglm-shrunken log2FoldChange and lfcSE side by side, ranked by the shrunken value; the p-values come from the unshrunken fit and shrinkage does not change the test. Report the DESeq2 / edgeR overlap from T1S2b as the high-confidence set. Report the hallmark GSEA table with database version, rank metric (Wald statistic), universe, size window and the leading-edge genes of each significant set, plus the GO BP second pass and the note that Reactome was unavailable. State the sample_01 verdict, its stated reason, and the with/without sensitivity result. Close with the limitations: n=6 per group detects moderate-to-large effects only, no independent validation cohort, enrichment is method-dependent, and gene-level counts preclude isoform-length offsets. Attach the full reproducibility record: sessionInfo, all package versions, the permutation seed, and the gene set collection version.
steps.context: Synthesis of T1S1 (QC and the sample_01 verdict), T1S2 (DESeq2 DE and the depth sensitivity analysis), T1S2b (edgeR overlap) and T2S1 (hallmark and GO GSEA).
acceptance_criteria: The report names the method, package versions, design formula, contrast direction, thresholds, number of genes tested after filtering, and number of DE genes
MA plot and dispersion plot appear before the gene tables, each with a caption stating what it shows
The gene table carries unshrunken LFC, shrunken LFC and lfcSE together, ranked by the shrunken value
The DESeq2/edgeR intersection is reported as the high-confidence set with both individual counts
The enrichment section states the collection and version, the rank metric, the universe, the size window, and lists leading-edge genes per significant set
The sample_01 keep/drop verdict, its reason, and the with/without sensitivity comparison are stated explicitly
A limitations section states the n=6 power limit, the absence of a validation cohort, the method-dependence of enrichment, and the missing isoform length offsets
sessionInfo, package versions, the seed, and the gene set collection version are stored with the results
constraints: Rank the gene table by the shrunken log2 fold change, never by the unshrunken value alone
Keep the p-values from the unshrunken fit and name the shrinkage estimator in the table header
Report the DESeq2/edgeR overlap, not the union
State that enrichment results depend on the method chosen and present pathway hits as hypotheses
Store the reproducibility record with the results, not as a separate note
Do not state a biological conclusion that the FDR-adjusted results do not support
caveats: Do not let a compelling pathway narrative outrun the gene-level evidence; if the DE list is short or the p-value histogram was irregular, that must lead the interpretation rather than sit in a footnote

grounding.reason: Report content follows the returned report-step rules: method/version/design/threshold disclosure (R-0041@059a), MA and dispersion diagnostics (R-0087@c53d), shrunken and unshrunken effects side by side (R-0085@c24d), two-method overlap (R-0042@54e1), enrichment provenance and method-dependence caveat (R-0051@01ca, R-0055@107a), leading edge per set (R-0105@c4a8), reproducibility record (R-0086@becf).
